description:
Compare two captured screens side by side: layout structure, page sections, observed actions,
dimensions, screen types, and design guide differences. Returns a structured comparison with
similarities, differences, and factual observations.

Use this when the user wants to understand how two products approach the same problem
differently—e.g. comparing Linear's pricing page with Stripe's pricing page, or Vercel's
onboarding with Notion's onboarding.

You can also compare one screen against a target description to see how close a reference
matches what the user is trying to build.

focus.description: What aspects to emphasize in the comparison.

screenA.description: First screen id to compare, e.g. linear-marketing-pricing.

screenB.description: Second screen id to compare. If omitted, provide targetDescription instead.

targetDescription.description: Instead of screenB, describe what you're building to see how screenA matches, e.g. "Pricing page with 3 tiers and a feature comparison table".

name: compare_screens

observations.description: Design observations and takeaways from the comparison.

report.description: Markdown summary of the comparison between the two screens.

kind.description: flow is an onboarding step, marketing a public web page, product an in-app screen.

screenB.description: Details about the second screen (null if comparing against targetDescription).

kind.description: flow is an onboarding step, marketing a public web page, product an in-app screen.

similarities.description: What the two screens have in common.

targetDescription.description: The target description if comparing against text instead of screenB.

title: Compare two screens
